cultural.vision_reason: This is a batik hand-drawn sarong (unsewn tube skirt) with a classic kepala/badan structure, sawat and floral motifs typical of Javanese/Balinese batik traditions; it is a garment cloth plausible for the region.

physical.title: skirt (unsewn); sarong (unsewn)
physical.summary: A batik tube skirt, a sarung, made from tabby cotton cloth; unsewn, hand-drawn.  Central kepala has triangles with alternating cream and light blue ground enclosing floral and foliate shapes in black and blue.  Black area between triangles with star and paku shapes. Sembagi-like pattern above and below in borders, which continue up outer side of papan.  Papan enclosed in frame of curlicue motifs in cream on black ground; papan themselves have phoenixes in same colour scheme.  Badan includes sawat shapes at an angle, also groups of squares with serrated edges in threes, fours, fives, sixes, sevens in various arrangements.  Background filled with gringsing.  All in blue/black on cream ground.  Red veining shows red dyed last.  [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
